> Thanks again for the time this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record.

Hi Alice / Rajesh — Vanessa from Infra here. Short technical responses and an initial artifacts bundle attached (pii-data-map.xlsx — template; redwood-deployment-diagram.pdf — baseline).

Answers to your Qs:
1) Egress blocklist/allowlist model: yes — our Private deployment supports a deny-by-default posture. Typical setup we recommend:
   - Customer VPC with no default route to internet; egress via a dedicated NAT/egress subnet only to explicitly allowed endpoints.
   - Security groups + host-level firewall policies to limit outbound ports.
   - We support integration with customer-managed firewalls (Palo Alto, Fortinet) or cloud-managed egress gateways.
   - Mutual TLS and signed certificates for service-to-service traffic to reduce risk of accidental exfil.

2) Airgapped/offline model import: we provide a signed model artifact package and an installer that runs in an offline appliance. Process overview:
   - Redwood generates a model bundle (gzipped, signed) and an integrity checksum.
   - Customer confirms checksum and runs local installer; the runtime has no outbound calls during import unless customer explicitly enables a staging NAT for verification.
   - We also offer an optional HSM-backed signature verification step for high-assurance customers.

3) Retention and logs: we can configure request logs to be retained for 90 days by default and offer on-demand purge APIs. For customers requiring immutable audit archives, we can stream hashed logs to a customer-owned S3 with encryption-at-rest and lifecycle policies.

4) PII handling: we recommend a layered approach:
   - Field-level classification and masking at ingestion.
   - KV cache and prefix caching disabled for any dataset marked as restricted-PHI/PII by policy.
   - Fine-grained RBAC on who can export request logs.

Attachments in this message: pii-data-map.xlsx (template for your team to fill), redwood-deployment-diagram.pdf (baseline mapping showing egress points and optional offline package flow).
